formats.intent: IntentPacket JSON (src/scholar_protocol/intent.py), the authored protocol; compile with scholar_protocol.compiler.compile_protocol
formats.protocol: compiled protocol.json (ResearchProtocol); used only for defects that exist at this level (criterion and question ids are generated by the compiler from an intent)

severity_scale_note: The set's own scale; the words follow .agents/skills/critic-contract/SKILL.md, the meanings are defined here.

severity_scale.critical: the review cannot answer its questions or cannot be screened as written
severity_scale.major: the protocol would bias or lose evidence the questions need, or contradicts its own scope
severity_scale.minor: the review still answers its questions, but the protocol is weaker, unclear or inefficient

base_notes.scoping: Generalization is left out of the search on purpose (stated in its rationale): a facet word in the query would hide the studies that never test it. Derived from the golden UAV scoping review (workspaces/golden-uav-30/intent.json), simplified: three questions, three concepts, three inclusions, three exclusions, four recall seeds taken from its verified records.
base_notes.sr: A companion systematic review in the same domain (UAV-guided versus uniform herbicide application). Its recall seeds are empty on purpose: the repository holds no verified record of a comparative spraying trial, and the set invents no DOI. A critic may mention the missing seeds as a note, never as a major finding.

fixed_check_catalogue.source: docs/ux/shared/final/02-checks.md, "The catalogue" (Inception and Discovery tables), read from branch dev/m10b/proposals-checks at 2d07228d7e10a1b7dc36260e2480a6f226d39624 (2026-11-15); not on main when this set was written

defects.defect: The second inclusion criterion keeps only studies whose method reached high accuracy, so studies that report failed transfer are removed before RQ3 can be answered.
defects.finding: INC-02 selects on a positive result, which biases the map toward success; RQ3 asks how failure and performance loss are reported, and the studies that report them are screened out.

defects.defect: The third inclusion criterion is mapped to RQ5, which does not exist (the protocol has three research questions).
defects.finding: INC-03 maps to RQ5, but only RQ1 to RQ3 exist; the mapping from criteria to questions is broken.
defects.check_note: The compiler accepts this; protocol validation reports CROSS_FIELD_RQ_REF. M10b's REVIEW_COMPILER_REFUSED compiles only, so it does not see it.

defects.defect: The first exclusion criterion excludes exactly what the first inclusion criterion requires (UAV images of an agricultural field), so no study can be eligible.
defects.finding: EXC-01 and INC-01 contradict each other: every study that satisfies INC-01 is excluded by EXC-01, so the included set is empty.

defects.defect: The second inclusion criterion admits literature reviews while the third exclusion criterion excludes them, so a review has two opposite verdicts.
defects.finding: INC-02 includes literature reviews and EXC-03 excludes them; the screener cannot decide a review consistently, and exclusion reasons will vary between screeners.

defects.defect: Screening is a single title-and-abstract pass, but the second inclusion criterion asks whether the methods are described well enough to chart how the model was evaluated, which only the full text shows.
defects.finding: With one tier there is no full-text stage, so INC-02 cannot be judged from title and abstract; either enable two-tier screening or move the methods-detail test out of the criteria.

defects.defect: A new inclusion criterion requires 20 citations, which is not stated in a title or abstract.
defects.finding: INC-04 cannot be judged from the title and abstract; citation counts are metadata that differ by database and date.

defects.defect: The same citation threshold cuts away recent studies: papers from 2025 and 2026 inside the stated date window have had little time to be cited.
defects.finding: A 20-citation floor works against the 2020 to 2026 window: the newest studies are removed for being new, which biases a map of current practice.

defects.defect: A fourth exclusion criterion repeats the third (reviews, editorials) under a different reason code, so the same record can be excluded for two reasons and the exclusion log counts it inconsistently.
defects.finding: EXC-04 overlaps EXC-03 (literature reviews and editorials) with a different reason code; merge them so one reason applies.

defects.defect: The weed concept has no synonyms, so the search misses the studies that say crop-weed, weeds, precision weeding or site-specific weed management instead of the bare word.
defects.finding: The concept 'weed' has no synonyms; compared with the other two concepts the query is much narrower here and will lose recall.

defects.defect: The UAV concept lists satellite, ground robot and tractor-mounted camera as synonyms; they are other platforms and the criteria exclude them.
defects.finding: 'satellite', 'ground robot' and 'tractor-mounted camera' are not synonyms of UAV; they change the meaning of the concept and retrieve the studies EXC-01 removes.

defects.defect: The search has no concept for weeds, although the title and all three questions are about crop and weed mapping; the query returns every UAV mapping study of any subject.
defects.finding: The word 'weed' is in the title and the questions and in no concept or synonym, so it is not in the compiled query.
defects.check_certainty: uncertain, may not fire: the title has 'crop-weed' (one token for the distiller's word pattern) and 'weed' alone is in RQ1 and RQ3; whether the check counts it depends on a tokeniser M10b has not built

defects.defect: A fourth concept, generalization, is ANDed into the query, so studies that never test generalization (the ones the map must show as a gap) are not retrieved.
defects.finding: RQ1 asks how studies evaluate generalization, including those that do not; an outcome term in the query removes those studies and the review will overstate how common generalization tests are.

defects.defect: The three concepts are merged into one OR group, so the query matches any paper about drones, or weeds, or detection, instead of requiring all three.
defects.finding: With one concept the compiled query has no AND; it will return a flood of unrelated drone, weed and detection papers.
defects.check_certainty: traced: exactly 1 concept (note level; the check names the symptom, not the merging)

defects.defect: The UAV concept joins its synonyms with AND, so a paper must contain UAV, UAS, drone, unmanned aerial vehicle and the other synonyms all at once.
defects.finding: boolean_operator 'AND' on the UAV concept turns the synonym list into a conjunction; the query will return almost nothing. Synonyms must be joined with OR.

defects.defect: The search starts in 2023 while the third inclusion criterion and the research scope say 2020 to 2026, so three years of eligible studies are never searched.
defects.finding: start_year 2023 contradicts INC-03 (2020 to 2026): eligible studies from 2020 to 2022 are not retrieved.

defects.defect: Two of the four recall seeds (2020 and 2021) fall before the search start, so the recall check can never find them.
defects.finding: The seeds 10.1016/j.biosystemseng.2020.10.001 (2020) and 10.1371/journal.pone.0251008 (2021) are outside the 2023 to 2026 window; the recall check would report them as missed for a reason that is not the query.

defects.defect: The search starts in 2027 and ends in 2026, an empty window.
defects.finding: start_year (2027) is after end_year (2026); no year can be searched.
defects.check_note: The compiler accepts this; protocol validation reports DATE_RANGE_INCOHERENT.

defects.defect: The second research question asks for a pooled effect size with a meta-analysis, which a scoping review does not do; the playbook and the rationale say the review maps designs and does not pool effects.
defects.finding: RQ2 needs effect estimates (pooled F1 differences), which fits a systematic review with meta-analysis, not this scoping review; the question, the synthesis and the review type disagree.

defects.defect: One recall seed is a literature review, which the third exclusion criterion removes, so the search is checked against a paper the review will not include.
defects.finding: The seed 10.1051/e3sconf/202568000077 is 'Review of AI methods in precision agriculture' (a review); EXC-03 excludes reviews, so it is not a valid recall target.
defects.check_note: RECALL_SEED_MISSED reads harvest results; no fixed check compares the seeds with the criteria.

defects.defect: Only one recall seed is kept, which says almost nothing about whether the query reaches the literature that matters.
defects.finding: One seed is too few to test the recall of a three-concept query; keep at least three.

defects.defect: The planned corpus is 20 to 40 records, while a three-concept search of four to five databases over 2020 to 2026 returned about a thousand records in the repository's own golden harvest.
defects.finding: The planned maximum (40) is far below what the query returns; either the query is meant to be much narrower or the plan is wrong. The planned size is advisory and never caps retrieval, so the harvest will simply be larger than planned.
defects.check_certainty: partial: the check needs the size estimate (a discovery step), it cannot fire on the protocol alone
defects.check_note: Evidence for the order of magnitude: workspaces/golden-uav-30 (pool_max 1000) and docs/ux/shared/final/02-checks.md (1,074 records harvested on 2026-11-13).

defects.defect: The planned corpus is 5,000 to 20,000 records for a scoping review of one narrow topic whose three-concept query returns about a thousand.
defects.finding: A planned minimum of 5,000 is out of proportion with a query of this shape and with a six-week scoping review that screens each record.

defects.defect: The unit of analysis is empty, so the protocol does not say what a row of the evidence map is.
defects.finding: unit_of_analysis is empty; the review does not say what one row of its evidence map is.
defects.check_certainty: traced: draft field unit_of_analysis empty is a blocker (DRAFT_INCOMPLETE)

defects.defect: The unit of analysis is farms and farmers, but the questions and criteria are about published studies and datasets.
defects.finding: unit_of_analysis (farms and farmers) does not match RQ1 to RQ3 or the criteria, which select published studies; the charting unit is undefined.

defects.defect: No criterion states the setting any more: agricultural fields are not required and forestry, urban and aquatic vegetation are not excluded, so weed mapping outside agriculture is eligible.
defects.finding: The context of the review (agricultural fields) is missing from INC-01 and EXC-02; invasive aquatic weeds or forestry mapping would be included.

defects.defect: The protocol has no exclusion criterion.
defects.finding: There is no exclusion criterion; the tool requires at least one, and without any an excluded record carries no stated reason.

defects.defect: All three exclusion criteria carry the same reason code OUT_OF_SCOPE, so the exclusion log cannot tell wrong platform, wrong task and wrong report type apart.
defects.finding: Three exclusions share one reason code; PRISMA-ScR reports exclusion reasons, and a single code makes the flow diagram uninformative.

defects.defect: The protocol defines no charting columns, although RQ2 and RQ3 can be answered only by extracting dataset, split and failure details.
defects.finding: matrix_dimensions is empty; with two-tier screening nothing will be extracted, and the scoping review has no charting form for RQ2 or RQ3.
defects.check_note: Protocol validation warns WARN_NO_MATRIX_DIMS (two_tier_screening is true).

defects.defect: The extraction form has no weed control or yield column, so RQ2 (weed control efficacy or crop yield) cannot be answered even from trials that report them.
defects.finding: No matrix dimension captures weed control efficacy or crop yield; RQ2 has no extraction target and nothing will flag the gap.

defects.defect: No criterion requires a uniform-application control arm any more, so single-arm trials and before-after reports are eligible, and a saving cannot be computed from them.
defects.finding: RQ1 and RQ2 are comparisons with uniform application; INC-02 and EXC-02 no longer require the control arm, so eligible studies may have no comparator.

defects.defect: The population is undefined: the unit of analysis is just 'Studies', and neither RQ1 nor INC-01 names a crop or field setting, so non-crop, forestry and amenity trials qualify.
defects.finding: Population is missing: no crop, cropping system or field setting is stated in the unit of analysis, RQ1 or INC-01, so pooled savings may mix arable fields with unrelated settings.

defects.defect: The third inclusion criterion accepts any language, but the search language limit is English only, so non-English trials are never retrieved.
defects.finding: INC-03 says any language and languages is ['en']; the search limit contradicts the stated scope and introduces a language bias the protocol does not acknowledge.

defects.defect: A new inclusion criterion asks for high methodological quality without any scale, tool or threshold.
defects.finding: INC-05 ('high methodological quality') has no operational definition; two screeners will disagree. Quality belongs in a risk-of-bias assessment (an extraction column), not in an eligibility criterion.

defects.defect: Two inclusion criteria carry the id INC-01, so a decision recorded against INC-01 is ambiguous.
defects.finding: The id INC-01 appears twice; criterion ids must be unique so that every decision names one criterion.
defects.check_note: Protocol validation reports DUPLICATE_CRITERION_ID. In the inception path ids are generated, so the fixed checks never see a duplicate.

defects.defect: The second inclusion criterion is named inc-01 and the first INC-01; ids that differ only by case are easily confused and may collide in a case-insensitive store.
defects.finding: 'inc-01' and 'INC-01' are distinct strings to the validator but the same label to a reader or a case-insensitive file system.
defects.check_note: Protocol validation passes: it compares ids exactly.

defects.defect: The search has no UAV concept although the title and RQ1 are about UAV weed maps; the query finds site-specific spraying trials guided by any sensor or none.
defects.finding: 'UAV' is in the title and in the questions and in no concept or synonym; the trials the review is about are not distinguished from other site-specific spraying.
defects.check_certainty: traced: UAV is an all-capitals acronym of 3 letters and occurs in no concept after removal

defects.defect: The site-specific application concept gets the synonyms weed control, herbicide application and spraying, which also describe ordinary uniform spraying and change the meaning of the concept.
defects.finding: 'weed control', 'herbicide application' and 'spraying' are not synonyms of site-specific application; the concept now matches the uniform-application arm and unrelated agronomy.

defects.defect: No start year is set, while the fourth inclusion criterion says 2010 or later, so the search and the criteria cover different years.
defects.finding: start_year is empty; the search window has no lower bound but INC-03 says 2010 or later.
defects.check_certainty: partial: the check is written for the draft (first search uses 2000), the compiled protocol simply has a null start year

defects.defect: The protocol is typed as a scoping review, but its questions ask for a quantified comparison of two arms with a random-effects meta-analysis.
defects.finding: playbook_type SCOPING_REVIEW does not fit RQ1 and RQ2 (pooled herbicide savings, a meta-analysis); the review is a systematic review, and the scoping presets (pool size, framework, two-tier defaults) do not apply.

defects.defect: No planned corpus size is stated, so the playbook preset (500 to 2,000 records) is applied without anyone choosing it.
defects.finding: pool_min and pool_max are absent, so the preset (500 to 2,000) is silently used; state a planned size for this question.

defects.defect: The three concepts are merged into one OR group, so the query matches any drone, herbicide or trial paper.
defects.finding: One concept means no AND: the query floods with unrelated papers.

defects.defect: The planned corpus is 20 to 60 records, while a flooding query returns far more; the planned size is advisory and nothing stops the harvest at 60.
defects.finding: pool_max 60 is out of proportion with the query: the harvest will be far larger than planned and the plan will not hold.
defects.check_certainty: partial: the check needs the size estimate (a discovery step)

defects.defect: The paradigm is Interpretivist, but the questions and the rationale call for pooling quantitative trial outcomes in a meta-analysis.
defects.finding: primary_paradigm 'Interpretivist' contradicts RQ1 to RQ3 (meta-analysis, meta-regression) and the rationale, which argues for a positivist stance.
